pages.SEO description -text: This is an app I've written to demonstrate the Central Limit Theorem in statistics.  I use rolling dice as an example and take the sum of the faces. It is an interactive simulation that rolls `N` dice, `T` times where each roll is remembered and displayed.

This is an app I wrote to demonstrate the Sieve of Eratosthenes.  It animates the algorithm, and the animation can be interacted with.  The app also has a module that generates what I call The Novelties.  This is a non-positional numbering system based on prime factorizations. Numbers are represented by their prime factorizations, but the primes are represented by their index in a list of primes.

The Sieve of Eratosthenes is an ancient algorithm for finding prime numbers. It does not test for primality, but it is capable of generating a list of all prime numbers from 2 to `n` with only addition.

pages.SEO description -text:
The Novelties are the integers represented with a non-positional number system.  Each integer is written as a concatenation of all prime factors in its prime factorization, including multiplicity.  The twist is that the primes are represented by their index in the set of  all primes.
The Novelties are ordered based on the length of their concatenation. Since primes are 'atomic', they are the smallest numbers. The largest numbers will always have the length of the largest power of 2 in the set.

The Central Limit Theorem is a theorem of huge importance in statistics. It says that if you sample an experiment enough times, then the average of those samples will be a normal random variable even if the random variable of the experiment itself was not normal.
